column1: # Every pattern is EXTRACTED, never transcribed: each instruction is
# assembled by riscv64-elf-as with all registers and immediates set to
# zero, so the bits that remain set are exactly the opcode and funct
# fields. tools/check-toolchain.sh verifies that assembler against a
# hand derivation from the pinned specification PDF.
# `fields` gives one entry per operand slot: kind, the bits that slot
# occupies, and a value-bit>encoding-bit map, all found by varying that
# slot alone. No RISC-V format table is
# written down anywhere — R/I/S/B/U/J are observed, not asserted.
# Operand shapes were found by trying candidates until one assembled —
# the assembler is the judge. Do not edit by hand; rerun the generator.
# `width` is the operand size in bits, and it is the one column NOT
# extracted from the assembler: `lb` and `ld` differ only in funct3 and
# nothing in the encoding says funct3=0 means one byte. It comes from the
# base ISA's naming and is checked by comparing bytes against GNU as.
# `converts` is the pair of types an `fcvt` moves between, in doc 02
# §2.5's names. It is the one distinction no operand carries: both
# `fcvt.w.s` and `fcvt.w.d` write an integer register from a float one.
